notes:
Deal status: closed-lost to direct OpenAI API (brand + speed of implementation).

Summary bullets:
- Customer: mid-market KM platform building an in-app chat + search assistant for enterprise customers. Primary drivers: low-latency answers, high-quality summarization, predictable unit economics.
- Timeline: POC kickoff 2025-11-18 (call id ff_20251118_1182X). 3-week POC; Redwood provided hosted API + optimize recommendations. Security & procurement engaged late Dec.
- What we delivered: hosted performance benchmarks, cost projection with batching & caching, canary rollout plan, SSO integration plan (SAML). Demo on 2025-12-03 with AE + SE. SE (Marco) led technical deep dive (LLM routing, KV cache).
- Customer feedback during eval: liked Redwood's observability & cost tooling but said integration complexity for their self-serve roadmap felt heavier than competitor. Quote from VP product: "We need something that our small infra team can ship in weeks — brand familiarity matters to our execs."
- Security review: Redwood provided SOC2 + draft SAML flow. Security raised concern about 3rd-party vendor onboarding cycle and preferred vendor with existing enterprise contracts. They noted vendor legal/vendor risk team had existing playbooks for OpenAI.
- Procurement outcome: procurement favored direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs citing simpler billing, smaller integration surface, faster POC. Also an internal budget freeze in Jan slowed approval; final procurement decision in Feb went to OpenAI.
- Internal dynamics: champion (Sr. PM Rachel Park) switched teams in Jan — left a gap in internal advocacy. No clear replacement. Sales attempted exec-level sponsor intro but hit closed door.
- Post-mortem notes: primary loss reasons = brand preference (OpenAI), perceived simpler developer path, stalled internal champion, and Jan budget freeze. Secondary: Redwood's dedicated/VPC story seen as more than they needed for initial rollout.
